title: ticket-inspector
owner: CC owns the tool, its checks, and its proofs. Akien owns the disposition of findings the tool surfaces
intention: A ticket inspector that checks every ticket in CairnCommons/tickets/ for structural completeness at its cursor position, producing findings per ticket in the same shape the build_inspector uses.
why: MEASURED 2026-08-26: 305 findings across 79 of 86 not-done tickets, 16 defect classes. The build loop stalls re-discovering what is missing from each ticket — 33 BUILDME tickets have no how field, 52 have no chart_claim, 34 have no sorted_berth. Most tickets were cast by hand before the sorted door existed, so the standing corpus was never retroactively checked. The sorted door checks at cast time; nothing checks at rest. This is the ticket-side counterpart of build_inspector.
traces_to: Law 3 — nothing is known until measured. Ticket completeness is unmeasured: 305 findings discovered only by ad-hoc audit.
Law 4 — a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy. The ticket field requirements exist as prose in CLAUDE.md and the sorted skill; nothing enforces them on standing tickets.
Law 1 — the resolver is spent on the novel, not on re-deriving the settled. The build loop stalls re-discovering what is missing from each ticket.

proves_green.proof_gate: tester runs proofs: each defect class fires on a fixture ticket exhibiting that defect and stays quiet on a clean ticket; the corpus sweep produces findings matching the audit count (or names the delta); the tool is importable and callable from CLI
proves_green.durability_gate: git commit — cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/ and its proofs committed and pushed

falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) a ticket at BUILDME with no how field passes silently; (2) a ticket past THINKME with no sorted_berth (and no 'none, because') passes silently; (3) prose children entries are not flagged; (4) a child ticket reference that resolves to no file is not flagged; (5) the tool is built as build_inspector's private check when the population is tickets, not code; (6) findings do not carry the ticket id and defect class.
falsifier.horizon: One build — the prototype exists as ticket_audit.py, the check roster is enumerated, and the build_inspector's sieve/roster pattern is settled.

how: A Python tool at cairn/tools/ticket_inspector/ with a roster of checks, same architecture as build_inspector's sieve families. Two check families: (1) field-presence — sorted_berth, intent_berth, gates, node_class, traces_to, watchme, intention, state, falsifier required past their cursor threshold (or explicit 'none, because'); (2) cursor-gated — chart_claim and how required at BUILDME+, children must be ticket IDs not prose, child tickets must exist on disk, owning_intention path must resolve, state string must match node_class workflow. Deterministic, no LLM. Callable from CLI (cairn tickets) and composable by the sorted door and build loop.
workflow_and_state: code-seam@v2: THINKME -> TICKETME -> BUILDME -> PROVEME -> WATCHME(the-corpus-gets-cleaner) -> [PROVED]

watchme.trigger: every commit to CairnCommons/tickets/ — the tool runs and its finding count is compared to the previous run
watchme.enough: the finding count drops below 50 (from the current 305) and stays there for 10 consecutive runs
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against this ticket's falsifier, carrying finding counts per run and the delta
watchme.consumer: the build loop and Akien at triage

chart_claim: validate-20260827T184722-c960f78eaf2a — chart chain complete with real content; verdict berthed at verdict-20260827T185207-83a1a2d0ff69
dependencies: CairnCommons/node_classes/ — the check roster reads the workflow definitions to know which fields are required at which cursor. code-seam.json and concept-piece.json are the two classes with standing tickets.
